newsitem.title: USA: Midwest Express sees pressure on earnings.
newsitem.headline: Midwest Express sees pressure on earnings.

text.p: Midwest Express Holdings Inc said Wednesday that an unscheduled engine repair, the return of the federal excise tax and competitive pricing pressure will negatively impact the company's quarterly earnings.
No other details were immediately available.
The carrier reported its June load factor for Midwest Express Airlines operations was 70.0 percent, up from 69.5 percent in the same month a year ago.

Traffic at Midwest Express Airlines in June rose 22 percent from a year ago to 130.9 million revenue passenger miles. Available seat miles (ASMs) increased 21.2 percent to 187.2 million. Passengers boarded increased 18.6% to 153,767 from 129,687 in June last year.
At its Skyway Airlines operations, the load factor for June was 46.8 percent, down from 48.6 percent in June 1996, the company said in a news release.

For the month of June 1997, Skyway Airlines traffic fell 1.9 percent to 6.1 million revenue passenger miles. Available seat miles increased 1.8 percent to 13.1 million. Passengers boarded during the month fell 1.4 percent to 27,795.

Midwest Express is the holding company for Midwest Express Airlines, a premium-service airline headquartered in Milwaukee and Skyway Airlines, which serves 24 cities, providing passengers with connections to Midwest Express. ((Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8787))
